ops.body: Origin: round-9 refuter finding on a93f14f5 (pre-existing detach architecture, NOT introduced by the A3.x series). A harness-level kill — SIGKILL, SIGTERM without unwind, or launchctl bootout during a nightly reinstall (bootout kills only the job's process GROUP; the detached Claude proposal process is deliberately in its own session, detach.py:68) — orphans a live BILLING process with zero accounting trace: no Python unwinds, so neither propose()'s handlers nor the A3.10 epilogue run; tracking is in-memory ProposalRecovery.run plus a fresh random UUID process name per attempt; restart scans only accounting artifacts, so the orphan's spend is permanently invisible. Cites: driver.py:216/289, launchd.py:139-150. Scoping decision (recorded on epic 49951f5): this does NOT block the current release (consumers are train/judge/golden/preflight; the research loop has no unattended production deployment until A6b) but HARD-BLOCKS A6b — the launchd campaign mode is the only place the trigger exists. Fix folds naturally into A7's watchdog scope (liveness monitoring and the registry are siblings).
